nodes.comment: TUI / IDE doctrine: LBE is not a thin CLI or a tool launcher. The CLI/TUI is the IDE/runtime surface for a doctrine-driven engineering agent. Models provide intelligence; LBE provides workspace context, operational doctrine, governance, evidence standards, capability orchestration, and durable engineering memory. The UI should be objective-driven rather than tool-driven: show Objective, Active Mode, Doctrine, Progress, Uncertainty, Evidence, Decisions, and Next Action; keep raw tool execution secondary. Modes are runtime doctrines, not tool presets. Engineering mode builds within authority. Audit mode establishes truth: evidence first, documentation allowed, implementation changes disabled unless explicitly authorized, ask the user when intent is missing, and never invent certainty. Investigation mode follows evidence without silently becoming implementation. Rule overload must be avoided: patterns can be advisory, warning, justification-required, or hard-blocking only when governance/security requires it. The agent should read relevant LBE knowledge when entering a workspace so its operating approach adapts to LBE, while deterministic Core authority remains separate and controls consequences. Mode changes should be visibly communicated in the UI—for example Audit may briefly present Evidence First / Documentation Allowed / Code Modification Disabled—then return to the workspace with that doctrine visibly active. The user assigns an engineering role and objective; they should not manually operate internal tools.
